newsitem.title: JORDAN: Kuwait-based shipping line increases Aqaba service.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait-based shipping line increases Aqaba service.

text.p: The Kuwait-based United Arab Shipping Company (UASC) is increasing its use of Jordan's Red Sea port of Aqaba to include transhipment of cargo to Jeddah, the company's agent in Jordan said on Wednesday.

Talal Halawani, manager of Jordan's Maltrans, said three large UASC container vessels will offload Jeddah-bound cargo in Aqaba this week for transhipment by a fourth UASC vessel to the Saudi port by the end of the month.
"They will enhance the transhipment service in the Red Sea," Halawani said adding that UASC may offload in Aqaba further Jeddah bound cargo.
UASC, jointly owned by Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain and Qatar, is the largest Arab shipping company.

The Kuwait-based company suspended service to Aqaba in 1990 after Iraq's invasion of Kuwait and Jordan's perceived sympathy with Baghdad. In January it resumed a twice monthly service to the port -- part of its U.S., European, Indian subcontinent and Far East service.
The three UASC large vessels with over 1,000 containers on board are Mariyah, which arrived on Tuesday, Ibn Bajjah expected to arrive on Thursday and a third vessel possibly on Saturday.
